sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section establishes the clinical context by detailing the patient's specific presentation, physical exam findings, and family history. It analyzes why the case initially mimicked Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes, creating a diagnostic challenge regarding the appropriate classification of early-onset hyperglycemia.
subtopics: Patient demographics and presenting symptoms (polydipsia, polyuria, weight loss)
Physical examination findings: BMI, blood pressure, absence of acanthosis nigricans
Analysis of the multi-generational family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance
Differentiation challenges: Why this case does not fit classic Type 1 or Type 2 profiles immediately
Laboratory red flags: Hyperglycemia combined with glycosuria in a lean/non-obese patient

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of HNF1A-MODY and Renal Glucose Handling
sections.description: This section provides the necessary biological background to understand the unique mechanism of HNF1A-MODY. It focuses specifically on how HNF1A mutations affect pancreatic beta-cell function and renal glucose thresholds, explaining the hallmark finding of glycosuria disproportionate to blood glucose levels.
subtopics: Role of HNF1A as a transcription factor in liver, kidney, and pancreas
Mechanism of beta-cell failure: Impaired insulin gene expression and GLUT2 regulation
Renal physiology: Reduced SGLT2 expression leading to lowered renal threshold for glucose
Why glycosuria occurs at relatively lower blood glucose concentrations compared to T2D/T1D
Progression of beta-cell dysfunction over time in HNF1A-MODY

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: From Biochemistry to Molecular Confirmation
sections.description: This section traces the step-by-step clinical logic used to rule out common etiologies and confirm MODY. It details the utility of autoantibody panels, C-peptide dynamics during stress tests, and the pivotal role of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) in identifying novel variants.
subtopics: Interpretation of Autoantibody Panels (GADA, IA-2A): Ruling out autoimmune destruction
'Glucagon Stimulation Test': Assessing residual beta-cell reserve vs. absolute deficiency
'Autonomic Neuropathy Assessment': Unexpected findings in early-stage monogenic diabetes
'Genetic Testing Strategy': Application of NGS panels for young-onset diabetes cohorts
'Variant Interpretation': Applying ACMG guidelines to classify a novel p.N270S mutation as Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Decision Making and Precision Medicine Implementation
sections.description: Focusing on treatment evolution, this section contrasts empirical management (initial insulin/metformin) with genotype-guided therapy. It discusses why Sulfonylureas are traditionally first-line but explores modern alternatives like GLP-1 RAs for this specific genetic subtype.
subtopics: 'Initial Empirical Therapy': Rationale for starting insulin/degludec + metformin/saxagliptin pre-diagnosis
'Transition Logic': Discontinuing insulin upon confirmation of MODY status and preserved C-peptide
